subtitle: Four-Band Dynamics
tagline: Four freely placed bands that compress or expand only where you need it, with an external sidechain, Mid/Side targeting, and zero-latency or linear-phase processing.

body.lead: TB Multiband Compressor gives you four dynamic bands that you place anywhere in the spectrum. Unlike a crossover-based multiband, the bands do not split the whole signal: each band works only on its own range, and the rest of the spectrum passes untouched. Gaps and overlaps between bands are allowed.

body.p: Each band compresses or expands, and its signed `RANGE` sets the direction and the maximum change. A band can listen to its own range, to a separate detector range, or to an external sidechain, and it can work on the stereo signal, the Mid, or the Side. `PROCESSING` switches between a zero-latency Dynamic topology and a Linear-phase mastering topology.

ul: Four bands placed freely from 30 Hz to 18 kHz, 0.25 to 4 octaves wide
Compression or expansion per band; the sign of RANGE selects downward or upward action
Threshold, ratio, knee, attack, release, and band output per band
Internal or shared external sidechain, with a band-linked or free detector range
Stereo, Mid, or Side processing per band, with adjustable stereo link
DYNAMIC (zero latency) or LINEAR phase, 2x to 8x oversampling, and 0 to 20 ms lookahead
Interactive band graph with the input spectrum and Delta Listen
20 factory presets, user presets, undo, and redo

steps: Gain per band (THRESHOLD, RANGE, RATIO, KNEE)
ATTACK, RELEASE, stereo link, channel mode

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Multiband Compressor 1.0.2 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build (AU and VST3) is version 1.0.1 and may differ.

ol: Insert TB Multiband Compressor on a track, bus, or the master. Init enables bands 1 to 3 at 120 Hz, 1.2 kHz, and 7 kHz with gentle compression; band 4 is off.
Select a band with the BAND buttons {{4}} or by clicking it in the graph {{3}}. Drag its node to set frequency and range, and drag a coloured edge to set the width.
Turn on `DELTA` {{7}} to hear only what the band changes, then turn it off again.

ul: Click a band to select it; double-click empty space to enable a band there.
Drag a node to set the band's frequency and range.
Drag either coloured band edge, or use the mouse wheel over a node, to set the width.
Hold the right mouse button on a band node for momentary Delta Listen; drag sideways to move the band while listening, and release to stop.
Double-click a value box to type an exact setting.

note.title: Latency
note.text: Only DYNAMIC with OVERSAMPLING OFF and LOOKAHEAD 0 ms has zero latency. The LOOKAHEAD / LAT label shows the current total latency in samples. PROCESSING, OVERSAMPLING, and LOOKAHEAD are not automatable, because changing them changes the reported latency.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows (hold to browse), or open the list to choose a factory or user preset. Save stores the current settings as a .tbmbc user preset. Undo and Redo step through recent edits. In the table, the band list shows the active bands; PROCESSING gives the phase mode, oversampling, and lookahead.
Kick Duck and Rhythmic Pump use the external sidechain, so route a key signal, such as a kick drum, to the plug-in's sidechain input.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

body.p: TB Multiband Compressor has 78 host parameters: six global ones and eighteen for each band. Band parameters are named Band 1 to Band 4.

rows: On for bands 1–3, off for band 4
Stricter, portable numeric state parsing. All 78 parameter IDs, the state and preset formats, and the audio behaviour are unchanged.
Response graph rework: RANGE now reads as the shaded base envelope, with the live gain reduction as an overlay tinted in the band colour; contours no longer draw over the 0 dB line.
First release: four independently placed bands with compression or expansion, signed Range, external sidechain, stereo and Mid/Side targeting, Dynamic or Linear modes, oversampling, and lookahead.
